why: A session starts from the handoff pack rather than from the PRD.
SEEN-104 wrote the pack; this is what makes reading it the default
instead of an instruction a session can skip.
The budget is a cap only if the session hears about it before it spends
the next turn. A warning after the fact is a report.
One matcher for both assistants: each matches on the tool names it has,
so the union names Edit, Write and MultiEdit on the Claude Code side and
apply_patch on the Codex side, with no per-client matcher to keep in step.
Ten seconds because this one runs in front of every edit.
Claude Code's alone: Codex documents no compaction hook, and an entry
naming one would be a command nothing ever runs. Both triggers, because
the automatic one is the one nobody chose and so the one that loses
the context.
Claude Code's alone, for the reason PreCompact is: Codex has no
subagent-stop event. Which agent stopped is read from the payload rather
than from a matcher, because the matcher on this event is not documented
as matching an agent name.

that read the journal and the generated copies, and none that walks
the tree.
